title: Coarse Menger Conjecture (Conjecture 1.1)
statement_text: For all integers $k\geq 0$ and $c\geq 1$ there exists $\ell\geq 0$ with the following property. Let $G$ be a graph and let $S,T\subseteq V(G)$. Then either there are $k+1$ paths between $S,T$, pairwise at distance at least $c$; or there is a set $X\subseteq V(G)$ with $|X|\leq k$ such that every path between $S,T$ contains a vertex with distance at most $\ell$ from some member of $X$.
context_text: Two independent groups — Albrechtsen, Huynh, Jacobs, Knappe and Wollan, and Georgakopoulos and Papasoglu — proposed this coarse analogue of Menger's theorem. It was shown to be true for $k=1$ by both groups, and for bounded-degree graphs with $c=2$ by Gartland–Korhonen–Lokshtanov and Hendrey–Norin–Steiner–Turcotte; however, the same authors of the present paper disproved it for all $k\geq 2$ and $c\geq 3$ in an earlier work.
attributed_to: Albrechtsen, Huynh, Jacobs, Knappe, and Wollan; and independently Georgakopoulos and Papasoglu
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture for all graphs of bounded path-width (and, further, for graphs of bounded coarse path-width); also notes the conjecture remains false for bounded tree-width.
paper_title: Asymptotic structure. V. The coarse Menger conjecture in bounded path-width

title: Informal conjecture: coarse Menger for bounded genus
statement_text: It might be true that the coarse Menger conjecture holds for graphs of bounded genus, that is: for all integers $g,k\geq0$ and $c\geq1$ there exists $\ell\geq0$ such that for every graph $G$ of genus at most $g$ and all $S,T\subseteq V(G)$, either there are $k+1$ paths between $S$ and $T$ pairwise at distance at least $c$, or there is a set $X\subseteq V(G)$ with $|X|\leq k$ such that every path between $S$ and $T$ contains a vertex at distance at most $\ell$ from some member of $X$.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple. Menger's theorem gives either $k+1$ vertex-disjoint $S$–$T$ paths or a set of at most $k$ vertices meeting all of them; the coarse Menger conjecture, proposed independently by Albrechtsen, Huynh, Jacobs, Knappe and Wollan and by Georgakopoulos and Papasoglu, asks for paths pairwise far apart: for all $k\ge0$ and $c\ge1$ there is $\ell$ such that every graph $G$ and $S,T\subseteq V(G)$ have either $k+1$ $S$–$T$ paths pairwise at distance at least $c$, or a set $X$ of at most $k$ vertices such that every $S$–$T$ path passes within distance $\ell$ of $X$. It holds for $k=1$, and for bounded-degree graphs when $c=2$, but three of the authors showed it is false for every $k\ge2$ and fixed $c\ge3$ (even allowing $|X|$ to be any constant depending on $k,c$). Their counterexamples have unbounded genus and unbounded path-width. In this paper the authors prove the conjecture for graphs excluding a fixed near-outerplanar graph as a minor, hence for graphs of bounded path-width (exclude a large tree) and for series-parallel graphs (exclude $K_4$), whereas it fails for bounded tree-width. The bounded-genus case is open; some progress is announced in a subsequent paper of the series.
notes: Stated as a possibility in running prose ("it might be true … but this is open"); no formal conjecture label.
paper_title: Asymptotic structure. V. The coarse Menger conjecture in bounded path-width
